question: Where will the great white shark Percy be on December 15, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Percy's last ping found was Aug 11, 2026 (Z-ping Aug 16) with no reported pings since; ~3 months silent. If he stays silent through Dec 15 (~50%), resolution is the August position, likely NY Bight/New England after a Jul 28 ping 14 mi off Long Island. If he pings again (~50%), December seasonality and his own prior winter (Gulf; still off Florida Jul 6) put him south of NJ with high probability. Due-west technicalities (points south of LI hit NJ; points south of MA hit RI/CT = Anywhere else; western Gulf could hit Mexico) spread mass. No human market found (only an unrelated Manifold extinction market).
calls.dossier:
- Percy: subadult male white shark, 9'9", 432 lb, tagged Jul 28 2025 Mahone Bay, Nova Scotia (OCEARCH/Tancook Islands) [ocearch.org tracker profile].
- Track history: from Nova Scotia down to the Gulf of Mexico in 2025-26 winter, then back up the East Coast; 4,660 miles total by late Jul 2026 [FOX Weather, Aug 2026].
- Question fine print: Jul 6 2026 ping had Florida due west (he was still off Florida in early July).
- Jul 27-28 2026: pinged off Sea Isle City NJ, then <24h later ~14 mi off Ocean Beach (Fire Island), NY [FOX Weather; NY Post/dnyuz Aug 2 2026]. FOX described him as appearing to head toward cooler northern waters.
- Search-indexed tracker snippet: latest ping Aug 11 2026 01:12; Z-ping Aug 16 2026 09:05. Location of the Aug 11 ping NOT found. No reports of any Percy ping in Sep, Oct or early Nov 2026 were found (searched several times).
- Live tracker could not be retrieved this run (JS page), so pings after mid-Aug cannot be ruled out.
- Peer sharks, early Nov 2026: Ernest (NS-tagged 2025) off New Jersey Nov 2; Penny in Florida Gulf waters Nov 2; Nori off Rhode Island Oct 31; OCEARCH says the southward migration has been underway since late Oct [Yahoo, Nov 4 2026].
- Status quo: if there is no new ping by Dec 15, the question resolves on the last (August) ping location.
- Base rates (not found as published data, built from general NW Atlantic white shark tracking patterns): mid-December positions of tagged juveniles/subadults are mostly the Carolinas to Florida or the Gulf, and some sit offshore or off NJ/VA. Over long-silent subadult tags, a gap of several months is common in fall, with a resumption often coming when the shark reaches warmer shallow southern waters in winter.
- Due-west geometry: a point ~14 mi south of Fire Island (~40.45N) has NJ (Monmouth) due west. Points south of Martha's Vineyard/Block Island (~41.1-41.3N) have RI/CT due west, which counts as 'Anywhere else'. Points east of Cape Cod have MA due west. The Gulf of Maine above ~43N has ME/NH. A western-Gulf point south of ~26N could have Mexico due west, which also counts as 'Anywhere else'.
- Resolution: resolves off the most recent ping on the OCEARCH Percy tracker page as of Dec 15 2026, not off news reports.
- Event window: a point-in-time snapshot on Dec 15 2026; as of Nov 8 2026, about 37 days remain for any new ping.
- Markets: none found on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold for this question.

calls.reasoning: Percy is a sub-adult male white shark tagged in Nova Scotia in July 2025. Last year he migrated south (Atlantic City Nov 23, Virginia Nov 24, 2025) and wintered in the Gulf. He was off Long Island on Jul 28, 2026, and the indexed tracker data shows his latest ping on Aug 11, 2026 (no location), followed by about 3 months of silence. I put roughly even odds on him pinging again before Dec 15. If he does, it will most likely be during the southward migration, so mostly south of NJ. If he stays silent, the question resolves on the Aug 11 ping. He was heading north from Long Island then, which spreads that case across NY, southern New England, MA, the Gulf of Maine and NS. Due-west technicalities move some mass to NJ and to 'Anywhere else' (RI/CT). No human market found; the only Manifold candidate asks about extinction and is unrelated.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agree on the facts: tagged NS Jul 2025; wintered south and reached the Gulf by Apr-May 2026; off FL Jul 6; Long Island Jul 28; latest indexed ping Aug 11, 2026 with no location; no Sep-Nov reports. They differ only on judgment: how likely a new ping is before Dec 15 (50-55%) and where the Aug 11 ping was (NY vs MA weighting). I checked: (1) a search for Percy's August pings again showed only the Jul 28 Long Island ping and the Aug 11 timestamp, with no location; (2) a search for a Nov 2026 Percy ping found nothing, and the Nov 3 migration articles don't mention him; (3) the Mapotic and OCEARCH tracker pages rendered without data; (4) a search for New England/NS pings again confirmed only the Aug 11 timestamp. None of the factual gaps could be settled. On judgment I take P(new ping) ≈ 0.5. Given a ping, about 75% south of NJ. Given silence, the Aug 11 spot is weighted toward NY and MA, since 14 days after Long Island he could be anywhere from the NY Bight to the Gulf of Maine.
